sources_considered.why: Third-party analysis that tests the $200B warehouse figure against NVIDIA's financials and buyer statements.
Reports Business Insider findings that Amazon stages NVIDIA racks in warehouses before power is ready.
Gives an independent estimate of sold vs. deployed AI compute and the lags between them.

receipt.public_excerpt: So, are $200 billion of Nvidia's chips sitting in warehouses? Nothing in Nvidia's sales or what its biggest buyers are saying supports that.

evidence_items.explanation: An analyst column finds no sign of a $200B glut in NVIDIA's numbers or buyer statements. It is commentary, not a measurement of idle chips.

receipt.public_excerpt: Amazon is taking ownership of Nvidia GB300 server racks before the data centers or power capacity exist to run them.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows one large buyer holding NVIDIA racks before power is ready, on the order of billions per month. This is far smaller than the claimed range and covers one company only.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Most AI compute probably doesn't go to frontier AI', paragraph 4

receipt.public_excerpt: If there’s a one-quarter lag between delivery and deployment, deployed compute at the end of 2025 would be comparable to sold compute as of Q3 2025, which was ~16 million H100e.

evidence_items.explanation: Epoch says it does not know how much sold compute is operational and models it with assumed lags. This confirms there is no direct public measure of idle chips.

unresolved_gaps: No public dollar measure of NVIDIA hardware sold since 2022 that sits uninstalled or unpowered.
Hyperscalers do not disclose GPU counts bought vs. GPU counts online.
